question: Describe how you would build our new public website on AEM Sites with Edge Delivery Services, including the blocks and page templates our marketing team will author with.
kb:
Our approach
- Your site is built on Edge Delivery Services and accepted for migration and launch, with authoring set up and Brand Visibility's edge routing working on your CDN.

How we would do it
- Turn the Brand Visibility findings and your search strategy into the site plan and information architecture, and agree the page set, templates and integrations.
- Design and build the block library and page templates on Edge Delivery Services, with the code managed and deployed from a GitHub repository.
- Set up authoring where your authors will work, in AEM Authoring, Microsoft SharePoint or Google Drive, with an instant URL to review and share changes.
- Agree the CDN route with your team, either Adobe's managed CDN or your own, then set it up and connect the agreed integrations.
- Build the agreed pages, testing each change for a Lighthouse score of 100 on mobile and desktop and against the agreed quality checks.
- Set up Brand Visibility's Optimize at Edge routing on the CDN, allow the AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 user agent in robots.txt and bot rules, and test the route.

What you get
- A working Edge Delivery site with the agreed pages
- Block library and page templates
- Configured authoring, CDN route and integrations
- Optimize at Edge routing, tested on the CDN
- Build record

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope.
- Planning estimate: 1,040 hours.

Risk we manage
- Scope growing during the build: we agree the page set, templates and integrations before building, and test each change against the agreed checks as we go.

- We will give each block in the library its Universal Editor definition, model and filter so authors can add and edit it in AEM, and check that pages publish to Edge Delivery as expected. The block code and styles stay in the Edge Delivery build.

question: Our current site runs on Drupal 9 and holds about 3,400 pages and 900 PDF documents, including state rate filings. Describe how you would migrate this content, what you would retire, and how you would preserve URLs.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Your current site runs on Drupal 9 and holds about 3,400 pages and 900 PDF documents, including state rate filings.
- Your agreed pages are on the new site with their titles, descriptions and structured data in place, and every retired URL redirects to its new page.

How we would do it
- Map your current site to the new one page by page, using your analytics and search data, and mark each page to keep, merge or retire.
- Run Adobe's importer on an example of each page type so your authors can agree the structure, then migrate the agreed pages into Edge Delivery documents and blocks.
- Carry over or rewrite titles, descriptions, headings and structured data for each migrated page, with your reviewers approving the rewritten copy.
- Build the redirect map, with every retired URL in the redirects spreadsheet, and set up bulk metadata and sitemaps for the new site.
- Run crawl, link and Lighthouse checks before launch, fix what falls short of the agreed thresholds, and test that every redirect resolves.
- Agree the site structure and paths with your team, and whether stage and production are split into separate sites.

What you get
- Migrated pages in Edge Delivery documents and blocks
- Redirect map
- Metadata and sitemap records
- Pre-launch check report
- AEM site created from the Edge Delivery template

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope.
- Planning estimate: 240 hours.

Risk we manage
- Losing search value when URLs change: every retired URL gets a redirect, and crawl and link checks must pass before launch.

question: Describe how you would make the new site conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, and how accessibility would be checked before each release.
kb:
Our approach
- With AEM, your content authors and site owners can create web content that meets the WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA success criteria.
- The Edge Delivery go-live checklist has you check that content and design conform to the specifications on your project's .aem.live domain, which may include accessibility checks.
- Your templates are tested against WCAG 2.2 Level AA before launch, and each release is checked the same way, with a record of the results.

How we would do it
- Agree WCAG 2.2 Level AA as the target with your team, then audit your current templates and a sample of pages and record each gap.
- Build each component and template to meet every Level A and AA success criterion, including visible focus, target size, color contrast, headings, form labels and text alternatives.
- Test every template with an automated scan, keyboard-only use and screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver, and log each issue against its WCAG success criterion.

What you get
- Accessibility audit of templates and sample pages
- WCAG 2.2 AA test plan and release checklist
- Issue log mapped to WCAG success criteria

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope.
- It sits beside our Implement AEM Sites on Edge Delivery, estimated in our answer to B.1.
- It sits beside our Go-live checklist and cutover, estimated in our answer to B.8.
- Planning estimate: about 60 to 240 hours for this work.

Risk we manage
- New content that falls below AA after launch: we train your authors and give them a checklist to run before they publish each page.

question: Describe how you would achieve and keep strong Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse scores on the new site.
kb:
Our approach
- On Edge Delivery Services, each pull request runs PageSpeed Insights against its test pages, and the AEM GitHub bot fails it if the score is below 100, with a small buffer for variation.
- In Adobe's Keeping it 100 guidance, the delayed phase of page loading holds third-party tags and other assets that are not material to the experience.

How we would do it
- Measure your current site's Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse scores for each key template, on mobile and desktop, as the baseline we compare against after launch.
- Agree a Lighthouse score per key template for release tests, and Google's good thresholds for real visitors: LCP 2.5 seconds, INP 200 milliseconds and CLS 0.1, at the 75th percentile.
- Build each template so what the first screen needs loads first and third-party tags load last, and check that the CDN caches pages, code and images.

What you get
- Baseline and target scores for each key template
- Third-party tag inventory with a load plan
- A performance test in every release

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope.
- It sits beside our Implement AEM Sites on Edge Delivery, estimated in our answer to B.1.
- It sits beside our Go-live checklist and cutover, estimated in our answer to B.8.

Risk we manage
- Third-party tags added after launch slowing pages again: we agree with your tag owners that each new tag passes the same release test, and watch real visitor data.

question: Akamai is our enterprise CDN and must remain in front of the site. Describe how you would configure Akamai with Edge Delivery Services, including caching, purging and security headers.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Akamai is your enterprise CDN and must remain in front of the site.
- Push invalidation is supported on Fastly, Akamai, Cloudflare and CloudFront CDNs as well as the Adobe-managed CDN, and is enabled in your project's production CDN configuration.
- On your own production CDN, the cache TTL is controlled by the origin's cache control response headers, and Adobe's setup guide says to enable origin cache control where the CDN offers it.

How we would do it
- Map your CDN setup with your CDN team: who owns it, the change windows, our access, the paths each origin serves, and which changes we prepare and your team applies.
- Build a stage configuration on your CDN that points each path to its origin, such as the Edge Delivery origin, whose cache headers set the TTL, or the AEM-managed CDN.
- Set up purging: push invalidation in the production CDN configuration on Edge Delivery, or for the AEM-managed CDN its purge API token and a matching purge on yours.

What you get
- Stage and production CDN configuration
- Load, caching, purge and page speed test results
- Security settings record signed off by your team

Timeline and effort
- This runs as the build closes, through testing, cutover and launch.
- It sits beside our Implement AEM Sites on Edge Delivery, estimated in our answer to B.1.
- It sits beside our Go-live checklist and cutover, estimated in our answer to B.8.

Risk we manage
- Changes held up by CDN access or change windows: we agree owners and windows in discovery and prepare each change for your CDN team to apply.

question: Every page that mentions rates, coverage or claims must be approved by our Compliance team before it is published. Describe the review and approval workflow you would set up for authors and reviewers.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Every page that mentions rates, coverage or claims must be approved by your Compliance team before it is published.
- Your authoring teams publish through one agreed process, and your brand and content rules run as governance checks on the agreed templates.

How we would do it
- Set the design-system and component standards every team follows, and write them up in a short standards guide for designers, developers and authors.
- Turn your brand and content rules into a brand policy in Governance Agent for your AEM or Edge Delivery authoring route, and test the checks on the agreed templates.
- Define the roles, approvals and publishing process with your content owner, so every page has an author, a reviewer and an approver.
- Run the change program for your authoring teams: training on the new process, playbooks for everyday tasks, and office hours through the first weeks.
- Inventory the blocks in your library, and agree with your authors which fields each block should let them edit.
- Agree the site structure and paths with your team, and whether stage and production are split into separate sites.

What you get

- Brand policy and governance checks, configured and tested
- Roles and approvals model
- Training materials, playbooks and change plan

question: We will not license Adobe Target in this phase. Describe how you would run A/B tests on the new quote-start page without it.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: You will not license Adobe Target in this phase.
- On Edge Delivery Services, an experiment uses the page you already have as the control, and a challenger page you create replaces it for some of your visitors.
- In AEM as a Cloud Service, the experimentation rail is the main way to set up experiments, on a project in an Edge Delivery Services context or in the Universal Editor.

How we would do it
- Agree a test plan with your team for each test: the hypothesis, one primary metric such as form starts, guardrail metrics, the sample size and the run time.
- Build the challenger as a copy of the control page that changes one thing, such as the headline or call to action, and keep it out of search indexes.
- Send the experiment ID and the variant each visitor sees into your analytics data with every page view and conversion, so each result can be split by variant.

What you get
- Test plan with hypothesis, metrics and sample size
- Challenger pages, kept out of search indexes
- Experiment and variant tracking in your analytics
- Results readout and learnings log for each test

Timeline and effort
- This runs every month from the month after launch.
- It sits beside our Implement AEM Sites on Edge Delivery, estimated in our answer to B.1.
- Planning estimate: about 20 to 80 hours a month.

Risk we manage
- Calling a winner too early on too little traffic: we set the sample size and run time before launch, and decide only when the test reaches them.

question: Describe your go-live and cutover plan, including redirects, search engine protection and rollback.
kb:
Our approach
- Your site goes live through a tested production pipeline, with CDN, SSL and DNS in place, redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria ready.

How we would do it
- Work through Adobe's go-live checklist with your team, giving each item an owner in a cutover plan.
- Run the production pipeline with functional and UI tests, complete Dispatcher validation, and set up notification profiles and traffic filter rules.
- Run performance and security tests on stage, which has the same sizing as production, and user acceptance testing on a test subdomain.
- Agree rollback criteria and redirects for retired URLs beforehand, then set up CDN and SSL and complete the DNS cutover.
- Agree the site structure and paths with your team, and whether stage and production are split into separate sites.
- Inventory the blocks in your library, and agree with your authors which fields each block should let them edit.

What you get
- Completed go-live checklist with owners
- Cutover plan with rollback criteria
- Performance, security and acceptance test results
- Redirects for retired URLs
- AEM site created from the Edge Delivery template

Timeline and effort
- This runs as the build closes, through testing, cutover and launch.
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.

Risk we manage
- A cutover problem with no way back: we agree rollback criteria beforehand and test on stage and a test subdomain before the DNS cutover.

What we would need from you
- Access to your DNS settings and SSL certificates, and the people who manage them
- Testers for user acceptance testing, and the person who approves go-live
- Access to AEM Author and to your Edge Delivery code

question: Describe how you would use Adobe Brand Visibility to measure how AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity describe Cedar Prairie and our products, and how you would report it to us.
kb:
Our approach
- Your CJA reports show AI-agent activity beside AI-referred visits and conversions, as separate measures reconciled to Brand Visibility and your web data.

How we would do it
- Configure the Brand Visibility connection with your CJA administrator, adding the Adobe Brand Visibility source dataset to a CJA connection and data view.
- Map the AI-agent activity's URLs and hosts to your site, and check the bot measures reconcile to Brand Visibility.
- Build a derived field on AI referring domains that identifies AI-referred visits in your existing CJA web data, reconciled to your agreed web reports.
- Agree the metric definitions with your application owners, and deliver a first report that keeps AI-agent activity and AI-referred visits and conversions as separate measures.

What you get
- Validated Brand Visibility connection in CJA
- Derived field for AI-referred visits
- Agreed metric definitions
- Initial report with separate AI-agent and visit measures
- Notes on what each measure covers

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope.
- Planning estimate: 56 hours.
- This needs CJA Select or higher.

Risk we manage
- Bot activity and human visits read as one number: we keep AI-agent activity and AI-referred visits and conversions as separate measures, each reconciled to its own source.

What we would need from you
- Access to your CJA connections and data views, granted by your application owners
catalog:
Our approach
- Brand Visibility sends aggregate AI-agent activity (from CDN logs, by URL and host) into CJA through an Experience Platform source. AI-referred visits and conversions come from CJA's own web data, and Brand Visibility reads those results for its business impact view.
- Brand Visibility runs the prompts you choose on a recurring basis across the AI platforms it supports and records how your brand appears in each answer and how that changes over time. It measures the prompts you monitor: the questions people put to AI assistants themselves are not disclosed by the platforms.
- Adobe's Brand Presence page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity as supported.
- The dashboards report the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned, how often your website is used as a source, share of voice and sentiment, and compare you with the other brands you choose to track in each market.

What we would do
- For Cedar Prairie Mutual Insurance Company, we will configure the supported Brand Visibility bot-data connection and map URLs and hosts; we will identify AI-referred visits in the existing CJA web data with a derived field on AI referring domains; and we will align observed AI-referral and conversion measures with existing CJA data.

What we would need from you
- Your Customer Journey Analytics package: CJA Select or higher.

question: Describe the program you would run to improve how Cedar Prairie appears in AI-generated answers, both on our own site and on third-party sites.
kb:
Our approach
- Each month, more of your pages give clear, sourced answers that people and every search engine see, with each change logged.

How we would do it
- Pick the month's pages from the agreed priorities and write a brief for each, with the question it answers and the approved facts it uses.
- Refresh the agreed existing pages and write the new answer page in your existing templates, with clear answers, supporting evidence, internal links and metadata.
- Run the agreed review rounds with your reviewers for factual accuracy and relevance, and publish the approved pages.
- Log each page change once, tagged search, AI or both, and check the published pages against their briefs.

What you get
- Page briefs with approved facts
- Published page refreshes and new answer page
- Page change log tagged search, AI or both

Timeline and effort
- This runs every month from the month after launch.
- Planning estimate: 64 hours a month.

Risk we manage
- Facts that drift from your approved sources: every page is written from the brief's approved facts and goes through your review rounds before it is published.

What we would need from you
- Source facts and reviewers who approve accuracy and relevance
- Publishing access and your existing page templates

catalog:
Our approach
- Brand Concierge answers only from the knowledge sources you configure (website pages, PDFs and product spreadsheets), not from general world knowledge. Website sources refresh on a schedule you set, so answers keep up with the pages you publish.
- When a question falls outside those sources, the concierge is designed to say it does not have the information rather than generate an unsupported answer, and guardrails can exclude topics such as legal or compliance matters.
- Before launch, it is tested against a golden set of real customer questions paired with ideal answers, including questions it should not answer; after launch, conversation transcripts are reviewed on a recurring basis.

question: When a visitor asks for a person, the conversation should pass to a licensed agent in our Genesys Cloud contact center. Describe how you would design this handoff.

Our approach

How we would do it
- Agree the route for Concierge data with your analytics team, either the bundled Concierge dataset or callback events, and document the dataset permissions.
- Bring the Concierge data into your Customer Journey Analytics through the agreed route, joined with your web or commerce data where permitted.
- Build Workspace reports for the agreed conversation, recommendation and purchase measures, limited to what the selected data supports.
- Add handoff rates where the handoff outcome has a documented source, a permitted ingestion and join route and a metric definition.

What you get
- Documented data route and dataset permissions
- Workspace reports on conversation, recommendation and purchase measures
- Measure definitions

- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope.

question: What uptime commitments apply to the proposed Adobe products?
catalog:
Uptime and recovery
- Adobe posts the availability of all its services at status.adobe.com.¹
- Edge Delivery Services: has the same service level agreement as AEM as a Cloud Service and runs on multiple CDNs, so delivery can switch to another CDN during an outage. Adobe acknowledges every incident within 15 minutes.²,³,⁴
- AEM Sites: a 99.99% service level is a separately licensed option, applied together with an Additional Publish Region on the same program. Sandboxes are not covered by the service level.⁵ Content can be restored from continuous backups within the past 24 hours or from system backups within the past seven days; a restore covers content, not code. - The uptime and recovery targets you need.
